Design Features for “Eco-Friendly” College Students

| Persona: "Eco-Friendly" | Sample Size: 292 Taiwanese College Students |
|:--------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| **TPB** | **Psychological Traits** |
| Attitudes | Deeply committed to sustainability |
| Behavioral Beliefs | Seeks rich provenance, CO₂e footprint, impact, worker‑welfare, and organic data |
| Subjective Norms | Motivated by eco‑peer norms and ESG transparency; high trust in ratings |
| **Design Implications** | **App Features** |
| Digital Product Passports | Show origin, CO₂e footprint, certifications, welfare badges |
| Transparency Tools | ESG reviews and governance scores, “Pre‑buy CSR review” toggle |
| In-Depth Mode | Customizable “Eco‑Deep‑Dive”: AI‑driven GenUI layouts for detailed vs. quick views, AI Q&A on pollution hotspots, company eco‑practices, and eco‑scores |

: Actionable advice designing features for “Eco-Friendly” college students

Design features for “Moderate” college students.

| "Moderate" Persona | 395 College Students |
|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Core Traits** | Motivated by health benefits and simple eco-wins (Attitudes) |
|  | Values simple, trustworthy cues, goal-setting, reminders (Perceived Control) |
|  | Responsive to light social and eco nudges (Subjective Norms) |
| **Design Implications** | Health-Framed Alerts: Pair sustainability scores with health risks/benefits (e.g. “–20% pesticides”); use healthy language, such as "eco materials", "eco packaging" |
|  | Goal-Setting & Reminders: Monthly intentions (e.g. “buy local”) with gentle push notifications, scores,nudges, e.g. push: “30% to your ‘buy local’ goal” (goal-setting), “Your Eco Score” dashboard, etc. |
|  | Quick-View Badges: “Top 5 Local Eco-Brands” summaries, e.g. “Top 3 Local Eco-Brands” / “5 Low-Pollution Picks” badges. Simple icons; deep dive only on tap. |

: Actionable advice designing features for “Moderate” college students

```{mermaid}
%%| echo: false

flowchart LR
    subgraph BeliefFormation [Belief Formation: Frugal]
        F_A[Attitude: Highly price-sensitive, eco must pay off]
        F_B[Subjective norms: Skeptical of eco trends]

    end

    I3[Intention: Act only if cost-effective options exist]

    F_A --> I3
    F_B --> I3
    F_C --> I3

    I3 --> F_Shopping[Shopping: Use cost-eco tradeoff slider]
    I3 --> F_Saving[Saving: Find local eco deals and coupons]
    I3 --> F_Investing[Investing: Accept micro-challenges for rewards]

    F_Shopping --> F[Outcome: Earn coupons/points for eco actions]
    F_Saving --> F
    F_Investing --> F
```

Design features for “Frugal” college students.

| "Frugal" Persona | 236 College Students |
|---------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| **Core Traits** | Highly price-sensitive; minimal extra info (low Attitudes toward eco data) |
|  | Prefers minimal extra info, uncomplicated choices (Perceived Control) |
|  | Skeptical, eco-actions must “pay off” (low Subjective Norms) |
| **Design Implications** | Cost–Eco Slider: Visualize “+30 TWD → 10% lower CO₂e” trade-offs |
|  | Local Deal Finder: Highlight flash deals, discounted eco-friendly and organic low budget goods nearby. Geofenced coupons for low-footprint groceries. |
|  | Micro-Rewards Challenges: Coupons or points for hitting “no-waste-week” or “plastic-free” or “meat-free day” mini-goals. One-tap “Accept Challenge” button; no pop-ups. |

: Actionable advice designing features for “Frugal” college students

### Disregarded Features

These type of social features universally received the lowest preference scores from all the personas.

-   Social Network, group challenges & leaderboards (TPB: subjective norms)

-   “Eco Friends” feed to connect classmates

I can't explain why social features scored so low. My own expectation was these type of features would be popular. This phenomena certainly deserves more attention and research to explain and disprove the findings.
